summary: The pollerBalancer.balance() method can unnecessarily block due to Go's non-deterministic map iteration order. When a poller's count drops to 0, subsequent loop iterations may grab another poller type's barrier and block instead of returning nil immediately.
userImpact: Workers may unnecessarily block on barriers even when they have no pending work, reducing throughput and potentially causing system hangs in certain scenarios.
rootCause: Go's non-deterministic map iteration order causes pollerBalancer.balance() to visit and grab the wrong poller type's barrier before checking the current poller type's count.
keyQuote: Due to random map iteration, the loop visits the other type (which now has count == 0 again) before the current type — grabs the barrier and blocks again instead of returning nil.
